newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on low volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on low volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed on low volumes Monday, with activity seen curtailed this week by the New Year holiday Wednesday.
"Very high open interest in February gold highlights a market set on the downtrend, but probably out of additional fuel to pressure prices," CRB analyst Terry Roggensack said.
COMEX February gold ended up 10 cents at $371.20 an ounce, after trading in a $371.70-371.00 range on total estimated gold futures volume of 12,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $369.25/369.75, against the London afternoon fix at $369.25.
"The sideways action in gold (in the last month) partially confirms the lack of decisive sentiment at work," Roggensack said.
But "we expect a major pivot point in the first week of January," he said. "Odds are growing that a failed break out downmove will confirm a major low in gold."
Spot gold saw three year lows around $366 an ounce in late November, after falling back from five year highs at $417 in February 1996.
The spot gold/silver ratio jumped Monday to end at 77.08, recovering from a three month low at 75.50 on Friday, reflecting the session's slide in silver prices.
COMEX March silver ended down 9.8 cents at $4.815 an ounce, after seeing an intraday low at $4.800 on total estimated silver futures volume of 15,000 lots.
Traders said some early trade selling had triggered stop orders below last week's low at $4.850, but there was no follow through later in the session.
"March silver is showing more signs of a bottom than gold, probably because it is more balanced with respect to open interest," Roggensack said.

The next CFTC Commitments of Traders Report is due Friday this week, but recent reports have shown Large Traders or funds holding near record net short positions in gold, but small net long positions in silver.
NYMEX April platinum closed up 80 cents at $375.90 an ounce, with the April platinum/gold spread recovering slightly to $2.50 an ounce, from $1.80 Friday.
NYMEX March palladium ended up five cents at $118.75.
